findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I found no release-blocking errors. The change follows the design: - The edited file and project root are canonicalized, and containment is checked with path.relative before anything runs. - golangci-lint runs once, from the package directory, on `.` with no `--fix`. The formatter runs only on the exact edited file. - One adapter freezes the configuration for every mode. Config discovery follows the upstream order: managed config, then the working directory, then the file's directory and its parents, then home. Upstream's base rules are applied before the working directory changes. One JSON config is written with relative-path-mode set to cfg, and it is exclusively created inside that original base. - Placeholders are replaced only where golangci-lint interpolates them. Relative resource paths and report destinations are made absolute against the original working directory. - Lossy YAML and TOML input is rejected rather than having values dropped. Keys are folded to lowercase the way Viper folds them. - Temporary-file cleanup is idempotent and also runs on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP, which re-raise the signal. - An older or missing helper produces a warning; it never falls back to the old per-file lint. Warnings are now kept alongside findings, and the 16 KiB cap includes a notice that not all findings are shown.  Tests use stubs that log the working directory and arguments, real-linter fixtures for the cfg, gomod, gitroot and wd modes, go.work, nested modules, sibling package tests and outside-root symlinks, and a CI matrix on v2.0.0 and v2.13.2 that fails if a tool is missing. The remaining issues are edge cases and gaps against the design's proof list, so they are recorded as non-blocking warnings.

Several proofs listed in the design have no visible test: (1) a real-linter check that a depguard rule using ${config-path} still reports a forbidden import, (2) a real-linter check that the normalized config still finds a relative ruleguard rules glob under cfg mode, (3) wd formatter exclusions, (4) a warning when the temporary config cannot be created, (5) a warning for invalid or malformed config, (6) home-directory precedence, (7) legacy YAML booleans against the real linter, and (8) a fixable non-format violation that stays reported. The code paths look correct, but these claims are stronger than what the tests show. Merge keys are only covered by a unit test, not a real-linter run.

normalizeReports always forces output.formats.text.path to 'stdout'. If the customer already sends another format (json, sarif, etc.) to stdout, the captured diagnostics will mix machine output into the agent's context, or golangci-lint may reject two formats writing to stdout. Either way the failure is visible as a warning, not a false clean result, but customer configs that only emit machine formats lose usable feedback.

diagnostics() treats an exit code of 0 as clean. A customer config with run.issues-exit-code: 0 will have its findings silently dropped from agent feedback (they still go to the text report). The old captureRemainingErrors behaved the same way, so this is not a regression. Conversely, a nonzero exit whose only stdout is a stats line such as '0 issues.' is shown as package findings instead of a loader warning.

The temporary config is written in prepareGoLintConfig before goLintProcess installs the signal handlers. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP arriving in that window leaves an untracked .safeword-go-lint-*.json in the base directory. This falls under the design's documented best-effort residue, but registering the handlers before the file is created would close the gap.

In normalizeGocritic, an empty ruleguard.rules string ('') becomes path.resolve(cwd, ''), i.e. the working directory itself. That turns an empty or disabled rules setting into a directory path. Empty comma-separated entries should be skipped.

saveTextReport rewrites the customer's configured text report on every hook run. It writes the package-scoped stdout even when the run failed with empty output, and it includes the in-memory truncation notice. As a result, the report file can no longer be trusted as complete output.

Other cwd-relative built-in settings that are not on the design's explicit list, such as issues.new-from-patch, are not normalized. They will now resolve against the package directory instead of the original working directory. The design explicitly limits normalization, so this is scope-consistent, but customers who use these settings may see different behavior.

I could not verify parity with the dogfood copy .safeword/hooks/lib/lint.ts, or the Cursor adapter after-file-edit.ts, because they were not in this packet. Their correctness relies on the CI parity check and the lifecycle tests that run them.
